$comment: ONE-SHOT corrective transition ledger. This is NOT a waiver, NOT an ignore list and NOT a severity override. It records exactly one transition between two named contract digests and the exact, complete set of breaking findings a named ruling accepted for it; any other comparison, and any added, removed or changed finding, keeps the gate red. Consumed only by ci/openapi-corrective-ledger.sh. Previous transition (#226, PR #227) is in git history.

transition.rationale: Owner ruling 2026-11-28 (tesserafin#129): a targeted, one-shot exception to remove contract properties nothing uses since the legacy playback chain, the shadow comparison and the Chromecast player were deleted - ServerConfiguration.PlaybackShadow, PlaybackSessionStreamDescriptor.ServedBy and .FallbackReason, and the Cast fields ServerConfiguration.CastReceiverApplications, SystemInfo.CastReceiverApplications and UserConfiguration.CastReceiverId. The gate stays strict: every finding is a property removal named by schema and property, with the evidence that it is unused.
transition.serverBindingStatement: No route, controller signature or accepted request changes: the removed request properties (POST /System/Configuration, /Users, /Users/Configuration) are ignored by the JSON binder when a client still sends them, and an existing system.xml or user configuration carrying them still loads with its other settings (MyXmlSerializerTests). Responses only lose the removed members.
clientsVerified: tesserafin-web main: no production code reads or writes these properties (web#323 removed the Chromecast player and the diagnostics page); the SDK is regenerated and the client type-checks and builds against the candidate contract
tesserafin-mobile main: no code references them; its pinned contract is unaffected
tesserafin server: no remaining reader; ServedBy/FallbackReason assertions removed from the E2E suites

findings.unusedEvidence: Consumed only by the Web Chromecast settings, removed with the Chromecast player (web#323); the Android client never read it. The Users.CastReceiverId column is dropped by an EF migration in this change.
